thread.title: China block of iPhone sales, memory outlook don't hurt chip stocks

author: morningstar.com
title: China block of iPhone sales, memory outlook don't hurt chip stocks
text:
By Wallace Witkowski, MarketWatch
Qualcomm patent violations cited in China block of older model Apple smartphones
Chip-related stocks outperformed the broader indexes Monday led by shares of as analysts weighed the effect of tariffs on the industry and China's order to stop selling certain older Apple Inc. iPhone models.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 1.2%, compared with a 0.3% drop in the S&P 500 index , a 0.4% fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Average , and a 0.4% gain in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index . Chip stockswere rebounding from recent selloffs that have pushed the SOX index down 6.5% for the year, compared with a 1.7% decline in the S&P 500, a 1.6% fall in the Dow average, and a 1.4% gain the Nasdaq.
Shares of Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) , which earlier in the session had been the best performer on the S&P 500, were up 2.4% after the chipmaker said the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court in China had blocked sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-court-orders-apple-to-stop-selling-some-iphones-2018-12-10) of Apple's (AAPL) iPhone 6S, iPhone 6S Plus, iPhone 7, iPhone 7 Plus, iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus and iPhone X in China because they violated two Qualcomm patents. Shares of Apple (AAPL) , which had been struggling, turned around and were recently up 0.5% amid reports that it would seek to appeal the decision (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/12/10/apple-files-appeal-to-overturn-iphone-sales-ban-in-china.html).
Blocked sales appear to be more harmful to Apple's suppliers, like Skyworks Solutions Inc. (SWKS), Qorvo Inc. (QRVO) and Broadcom Inc. (AVGO), according to Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh, who has a buy rating on Qualcomm and a $66 price target. Rakesh noted that the iPhone accounts for about 40% of Skyworks and Qorvo's revenue and about 15% of Broadcom's.
Skyworks shares declined 0.4%, Qorvo shares were down 2.2%, but Broadcom shares were up 4.1%. That muted affect on stocks could stem from the fact that sales of the newer iPhone XS/XS Max and XR were not affected.
"Assuming China [is about] 20% of iPhone sales, the impact to Skyworks, Qorvo and Broadcom would be 8%/8%/3% conservatively -- though we would note the newer XS/XS Max and XR are not impacted yet and risk should be lower," Rakesh said.
"The bigger risk is if Qualcomm could use this precedent to force a similar injunction in other geographies, (positive for Qualcomm but negative for the [radiofrequency chip] suppliers)," Rakesh said.
KeyBanc Capital markets analysts Weston Twigg also used the occasion to downgrade Skyworks and Qorvo to "sector weight" ratings based on weakening iPhone demand and weaker-than-expected smartphone demand in China.
Analysts at J.P. Morgan expect rough times for the chip and chip-equipment industry as memory chip prices keep falling well in to 2019, with the most bearish period being the first quarter, but considered the sectors a buy into weakness over the longer term. Micron Technology Inc. (MU), one of the biggest memory chip players, saw shares down 0.3%.
Eric Ross, Chief Investment Strategist at Cascend Securities, said growth in monthly sales of DRAM -- dynamic random access memory, the type of memory commonly used in PCs and servers -- has slowed to 10.2%, the weakest growth in the past five months, as customers burn off excess inventory.
Other chipmakers outperforming the SOX index were Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Applied Materials Inc. (AMAT), Intel Corp. (INTC) , and Texas Instruments Inc. (TXN)
-Wallace Witkowski; 1356ET
